title: reverseComplementRecord writes T into RNA records and is not an involution for RNA
description:
`reverseComplementRecord` (transform.ts lines 218-228) accepts RNA records; only protein throws. It always calls the DNA `reverseComplement` from seq/alphabet, whose table maps U->A and A->T.

RNA records do keep U:
- the GenBank parser's RNA_TABLE keeps U ("U kept for RNA");
- the FASTA reader treats "U without T" as RNA and keeps it;
- `types.ts` converts U to T only for DNA records.

So the reverse complement of an RNA record is written with T. Applying it twice silently turns every U of the original into T, so a user who reverse-complements twice instead of using undo permanently changes the stored sequence.

Biopython 1.88 disagrees. `SeqRecord(Seq('AUGCAAUUGN'), annotations={'molecule_type':'RNA'}).reverse_complement().seq` is 'NCAAUUGCAU' (it uses `reverse_complement_rna`); I ran this with the oracle venv.

Suggested fix: for molecule 'RNA', complement A to U (e.g. reverse-complement, then replace T with U), or reject RNA records explicitly.
expected: The reverse complement is 'NCAAUUGCAU', as Biopython gives for an RNA record, and reverse-complementing again gives back 'AUGCAAUUGN'.
actual: The test fails with: expected 'NCAATTGCAT' to be 'NCAAUUGCAU'. Reverse-complementing again gives 'ATGCAATTGN', so every U of the original has become T.

title: Inserting or replacing with an RNA record leaves U bases inside a DNA record
description:
`resolvePayload` (edit.ts lines 40-53) runs `normalizeDna` only on string payloads. A SeqRecord payload's `seq` is inserted unchanged, and mixing DNA and RNA is allowed because only a protein mismatch throws.

So `insertBases(dnaRec, g, rnaRecord)` and `replaceRange(dnaRec, r, rnaRecord)` return a record with molecule 'DNA' whose sequence contains U. That violates `types.ts` ("'U' is converted to 'T' for DNA records"). It also fails the implementer's own `recordProblems` check ("sequence is not uppercase IUPAC DNA").

The downstream effect is silent. `iupacMatches('T','U')` is false, so enzyme sites and primer binding sites that overlap the inserted bases are missed, and a GenBank export writes u into a DNA record.

The implementer's limitations note says "A DNA record can receive an RNA record", but not that the U bases are left in the DNA sequence. `concatRecords` rejects the same DNA/RNA mix.

Suggested fix: convert U to T when the target is DNA, or reject the mix as `concatRecords` does.
expected: The result is a valid DNA record ('AAAAGGTTCCCC'), or the call throws as `concatRecords` does for mixed molecule types.
actual: `out.seq` is 'AAAAGGUUCCCC' with molecule 'DNA', and `isDna(out.seq)` is false. `replaceRange` gives 'AAGGUUCCCC' in the same way.

title: Origin-spanning feature in two-segment join form leaves out bases inserted or replaced at the origin
description:
On a circular molecule, a feature that crosses the origin can be stored in two equivalent ways covering the same contiguous bases:
- as one wrapping segment, e.g. [18,23);
- as the INSDC join [18,20)+[0,3).

ops itself turns the first form into the second:
- `setTopology(circular -> linear)` splits the segment;
- `setTopology(linear -> circular)` keeps it split ("features unchanged");
- `concatRecords([plasmid], {topology:'circular'})` opens the plasmid at its origin and keeps the split.

`remapRangeWithPlan` (remap.ts lines 182-213) decides strict containment per segment (lines 200 and 206). An insertion at the origin (gap 0/L) or a replacement across it therefore never lies strictly inside either part. The inserted bases are left out, and the feature gets an artificial intron.

With the wrapping-segment form, the same edit extends the feature, as the spec requires: "treat an insertion at gap 0 as appending at L ... so a wrapping segment (e > L) grows". The implementer's report also says ops "handles both" forms.

Scientific impact: after a harmless topology round trip, a 1-bp insertion or a codon substitution at the origin inside an origin-spanning CDS is no longer covered by the CDS annotation. Its translation then hides the frameshift or mutation.

Suggested fix: treat a segment ending at L followed by one starting at 0, on a circular record, as contiguous when testing strict containment. Alternatively, merge such pairs into one wrapping segment when circularising in `setTopology` and `concatRecords`.
expected: The edit affects the feature the same way in both forms. Inserting G at the origin gives 'TTGAAA', as for the wrapping segment. Replacing [19,21) with CC gives 'TCCAA'.
actual: After the `setTopology` round trip, or after re-closing with `concatRecords`, the insertion gives 'TTAAA': the feature becomes [18,20)+[0,3) and skips the inserted G. The replacement gives 'TAA': the feature becomes [19,20)+[2,4) and skips CC. All three tests fail, e.g. "expected 'TTAAA' to be 'TTGAAA'" and "expected 'TAA' to be 'TCCAA'".

title: extractRange keeps /codon_start when it clips the 5' end of a CDS, so the fragment's CDS is in the wrong reading frame
description:
clipFeature/extractRange clips a CDS and sets partialStart (strand 1) or partialEnd (strand -1), but copies its qualifiers verbatim (copyFeature). When the number of clipped 5' bases c is not a multiple of 3, the first complete codon of the clipped feature lies at offset (3 - c%3)%3, so the INSDC /codon_start must become ((3 - c%3)%3)+1. seq/translate.ts translateFeature honours /codon_start (it is also written back by the GenBank writer), so the extracted CDS translates in the wrong frame and exports with a wrong /codon_start.

Reproduced on the committed pBR322_J01749.gb fixture:
- tet carries an explicit /codon_start=1; ROP and bla are also affected. bla is a minus-strand CDS, clipped at its right end.
- Clipping 1 or 2 bases gives garbage translations: 2 of 3 clip offsets are wrong.
- Patching /codon_start to 3 (clip 1) or 2 (clip 2) gives exactly full.slice(1), which confirms the expected value.

The second piece of a feature that extractRange splits on a circular parent has the same problem. In cloning simulations, any restriction fragment that cuts inside a CDS hits this (e.g. BamHI or SalI in tet, PstI in bla). The fused construct's translation, which users check for an in-frame fusion, is then shown in the wrong frame.
expected: The clipped CDS gets /codon_start = ((3 - c mod 3) mod 3) + 1, i.e. 3 for a 1-base clip and 2 for a 2-base clip. translateFeature(piece, clipped) returns 'KSNNALIVILGTVTLDAVGIGLVM...', the original protein minus its first residue.
actual: /codon_start stays '1'. The translation is '*NLTMRSSSSSAPSPWML*A*AWLCRYCRA...' for a 1-base clip and 'EI*QCAHRHPRHRHPGCCRHRLGYA...' for a 2-base clip. bla (strand -1, clipped at its right end) and ROP give the same kind of wrong-frame protein.

title: /transl_except positions are never remapped, so edits, extraction, ligation and rotation mistranslate selenoproteins silently or make translateFeature throw
description:
/transl_except=(pos:a..b,aa:X) holds absolute 1-based parent coordinates, and seq/translate.ts translateFeature applies it. No ops function updates it: copyFeature/copyQualifiers copy qualifiers verbatim, while the segments move in insertBases, deleteRange, replaceRange, concatRecords, rotateOrigin, reverseComplementRecord and extractRange.
- A shift by a multiple of 3 that stays inside the CDS silently overrides the wrong codon: Sec moves one codon and the real Sec TGA is read as a stop.
- Other shifts make translateFeature throw a TranslationError.

Real data, from the gitignored fixtures/large/ecoli_U00096.3.gb parsed with io/genbank. All three selenoprotein CDSs (fdnG, fdoG, fdhF) carry /transl_except.
- insertBases of 3 bp at the gene start: fdnG shows 'U' at residue 194 and '*' at the real Sec residue 195; fdoG and fdhF behave the same way.
- Extracting exactly the gene extent: translateFeature throws 'unsupported or out-of-range location'.
- rotateOrigin(rec, 1_000_000): translateFeature throws 'position outside the feature'.

The same applies to the /transl_except=(pos:..,aa:TERM) entries common in mitochondrial genomes. This is not among the listed known limitations.
expected: /transl_except positions move with the feature, or the qualifier is dropped or flagged when its codon is edited, so the selenoprotein still translates as 'MUK*' after an unrelated upstream edit, extraction, ligation or rotation.
actual: Inserting 'GGG' at gap 0 gives 'U*K*'. Extracting [3,15) gives 'M*U*'. rotateOrigin(circular copy, 12) and concatRecords([3-bp part, lin]) also give 'U*K*'. Inserting 1 base throws TranslationError ('not a codon of the reading frame'). On E. coli, fdnG, fdoG and fdhF are mistranslated after a 3-bp insertion, and translateFeature throws after extraction or rotation.

title: reverseComplementRecord writes T into RNA records, so U is lost and RC is no longer an involution
description:
reverseComplementRecord only rejects protein records. For RNA records it applies the DNA reverseComplement helper, which maps U to A and A to T, and keeps molecule 'RNA'.

io/fasta classifies 'U without T' as RNA, so RNA records with U are ordinary parser output: sgRNA, siRNA and miRBase FASTA all look like this. The reverse complement of such a record contains T instead of U, and applying RC twice changes the user's sequence permanently. The module's own tests assert the involution, but only for DNA.

Biopython 1.88 SeqRecord.reverse_complement, the module's own RC oracle, returns 'UAGCUCUAAAAC' for this input (run with tools/oracle/.venv on a SeqRecord with molecule_type RNA). The listed known limitation covers U to T in inserted text only, not reverse complement.
expected: 'UAGCUCUAAAAC' (an RNA reverse complement with U, as Biopython gives), and RC applied twice returns the original 'GUUUUAGAGCUA'.
actual: 'TAGCTCTAAAAC' with molecule still 'RNA'. Applying RC twice gives 'GTTTTAGAGCTA'.

title: The empty range {L, L} on a circular record is rejected by replaceRange, deleteRange, extractRange and remapRange, although gap L is accepted elsewhere
description:
types.ts allows gap positions in [0, L] for both topologies (0 and L are the same gap on a circle). insertBases(circ, L, ...) and remapGap(L, ...) accept gap L. checkRange, however, requires start < L on circular records, so the natural empty selection after the last base, {start: L, end: L}, makes replaceRange, deleteRange, extractRange and remapRange throw a RangeError.

This contradicts replaceRange's TSDoc: 'An empty range makes this exactly insertBases(rec, range.start, replacement)'. An editor that implements typing or paste as replaceRange(selection, text), the standard replace-selection pattern, throws when the caret sits after the last base of a plasmid. A UI that tracks an empty selection with remapRange throws on the next edit. Linear records accept {L, L}.
expected: {L, L} on a circular record is treated like gap L (equivalently {0, 0}). replaceRange equals insertBases(circ, 20, 'GG') ('AAAAACCCCCGGGGGTTTTTGG'), deleteRange is a no-op copy, and remapRange returns {0, 0}.
actual: RangeError: 'replace: range {start: 20, end: 20} is invalid for a circular sequence of length 20 (must satisfy 0 <= start < length and end - start <= length)'. deleteRange, extractRange and remapRange throw the same error.

title: extractRange cannot take a digest fragment's parentRange for a plasmid cut once, so ops cannot build that cloning intermediate
description:
enzymes/digest documents that a circle cut once yields one linear fragment whose parentRange is L + overhang bases long. For pUC19 + EcoRI that is {284, 2974}: 2690 = 2686 + 4. extractRange (via checkRange) rejects ranges longer than L, and segmentParts assumes len <= L.

The ops spec names cloning simulations as a consumer of this module. The natural way to build a fragment record with features is extractRange(parent, fragment.parentRange) plus the fragment's ends, and it throws for the most common cloning intermediate: a plasmid linearized with a single enzyme. The same approach works for two cuts: extracting both pUC19 EcoRI+HindIII fragments, setting their digest ends and running concatRecords(..., {topology: 'circular'}) reproduces the rotated plasmid exactly.

This is a contract mismatch between ops and enzymes/digest; one of the two sides needs to change, or ops needs a dedicated helper.
expected: ops can produce the 2690-bp linear fragment record, with features re-based and the overhang bases duplicated at both ends, from the documented digest output.
actual: RangeError: 'extractRange: range {start: 284, end: 2974} is invalid for a circular sequence of length 2686 (must satisfy 0 <= start < length and end - start <= length)'.

title: A gap of -0 (e.g. Math.round(-0.3)) produces -0 coordinates, which the module's own invariant check flags
description:
checkGap and checkRange accept -0. planEdit then stores start = -0, and remapGapWithPlan returns insertAt = -0 for zero-length segments at the edit point. This applies to insertBases(lin, -0, ...) and to deleteRange or replaceRange with range.start -0.

A UI that computes the caret with Math.round(x / charWidth) gets -0 for a click just left of base 1. The output then carries {start: -0, end: -0}, which the implementer's own invariant helper recordProblems reports as 'negative zero'. (-0).toLocaleString() and Intl.NumberFormat render '-0', so the coordinate panel shows '-0'. Normalizing with `+ 0` in planEdit fixes it.
expected: Coordinates are +0, recordProblems(out) is [], and the coordinate formats as '0'.
actual: The site becomes {start: -0, end: -0}, recordProblems reports 'feature s: negative zero in {"start":0,"end":0}', and toLocaleString gives '-0'.

title: The ops test suite is red: 8 failing tests and a tsc error, so the property tests barely run
description:
In the current tree the module's own suite fails, although the report says all 133 tests pass. Now there are 149 tests, 8 of them failing, and one ops test file has a TypeScript error.

Causes (each failing case was re-run and inspected):
(1) Five property tests compare every feature with `nonPositional(got) == nonPositional(f)` ("property: deleteRange > matches the token model", "property: replaceRange > matches the token model", "property: replaceRange > with a record replacement carries its features", "property: edits next to sticky ends", "property: insertBases > carries the features of an inserted record"). The implementation now adds or rewrites /codon_start when a CDS loses 5' bases. Example, seed 2001 case #2: deleteRange {1,123} on a 144 bp circle turns CDS strand -1 [83,177) into [1,23) with /codon_start=2. That is the correct frame (32 bases lost at the 5' end), but the test expects the qualifiers unchanged.
(2) The per-segment token model `modelSegmentTokens` does not know the new contiguous-run rule. Example, seed 1001 case #1953 (circular, L = 234, insertion of 12 bp at gap 0): f0 has segments [107,111),[233,234),[0,192). The implementation turns [233,234) into [233,246), absorbing the inserted bases; the model expects [233].
(3) "agree with the record edits" asserts that per-segment remapRange equals the edited feature's segments. This fails for adjacent segments (seed 4001 case #1660), see the separate minor finding.
(4) ops.regression.test.ts "fragment record of a singly cut plasmid" asserts that extractRange(pUC19, {284, 2974}) (L+4, the parentRange from digest) does not throw. transform.ts lines 171-176 deliberately throw RangeError for that range, so the regression test contradicts the documented contract.

Consequence: `forCases` stops at the first failing case. The deleteRange property group runs only 3 of 2,500 cases, replaceRange 9 and sticky ends 10, so the module's main safety net no longer checks edit semantics or overhang tracking. The spec requires green tests and error-free files.

The implementation itself is not at fault here. My own per-base models agree with it: 60,000 random insert/delete/replace cases including runs, origin-crossing deletions and sites; 50,000 sticky-end cases; 87,000 codon-frame checks. The tests need updating, plus a decision on the L+overhang range.
reproduction:
cd /home/srdgjuchdr/HHereditas/packages/core && npx vitest run src/ops
#  Test Files  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
#       Tests  8 failed | 141 passed (149)
#  x property: insertBases > matches the token model ... case #1953 (seed 1001): segment 1 of f0: expected [233, 1000000, ...] to deeply equal [233]
#  x property: insertBases > carries the features of an inserted record ... case #452 (seed 1002)
#  x property: edits next to sticky ends ... case #9 (seed 1501)
#  x property: deleteRange ... case #2 (seed 2001)
#  x property: replaceRange > matches the token model ... case #8 (seed 3001)
#  x property: replaceRange > with a record replacement ... case #8 (seed 3003)
#  x property: remapFeatures / remapRange / remapGap ... case #1660 (seed 4001)
#  x ops.regression.test.ts > fragment record of a singly cut plasmid: RangeError: extractRange: range {start: 284, end: 2974} is invalid for a circular sequence of length 2686
npx tsc --noEmit -p /home/srdgjuchdr/HHereditas/packages/core | grep src/ops
#  src/ops/ops.regression.test.ts(16,10): error TS6133: 'deleteRange' is declared but its value is never read.
expected: All ops tests green and no tsc errors in ops files, as the spec requires. The property models should cover the /codon_start rewriting and the contiguous-run rule. The regression test should agree with extractRange's documented RangeError, or extractRange should accept the range.
actual: 8 of 149 tests fail and ops.regression.test.ts has TS6133. Seven property groups stop after 2 to 1,953 of their 2,500 cases. The regression test asserts behaviour the implementation documents it will not provide.

title: Edits and extractRange leave a stale /translation on a changed CDS, and writeGenbank exports it
description:
remapFeaturesWithPlan (remap.ts) and clipFeature (transform.ts) already rewrite sequence-dependent qualifiers when a feature's bases change: /codon_start, /transl_except, /anticodon, /rpt_unit_range. They copy /translation unchanged.

Any insertion, deletion or replacement strictly inside a CDS changes the encoded protein, and so does a 5' clip by extractRange. The feature still carries the old protein, and writeGenbank writes it out. Typical cases are a point mutation via replaceRange, an in-frame codon deletion, or extracting a fragment that cuts a CDS.

INSDC defines /translation as the conceptual translation of the CDS, and NCBI's validator rejects mismatches. Tools that read the exported file, and any UI panel that shows stored qualifiers, will report a protein the DNA does not encode. NCBI GenBank records almost always carry /translation, so this happens on ordinary edits of real files.

For comparison, Biopython/pydna drop features that span an edit, and SnapGene recomputes the translation.

The qualifier is correctly kept, and should stay, when the feature's bases are unchanged: features moved as a block, rotateOrigin, reverseComplementRecord, setTopology, carried features and concatRecords.
expected: When an operation changes the bases of a feature (inserted/deleted/replaced bases inside it, or a clipped end), its /translation is dropped or regenerated, as /codon_start and /transl_except already are. For the L11W mutation the protein must read 'MKSNNALIVIWG...'. For the extracted piece it must read 'AGRIVAGITG...'.
actual: The /translation qualifier is copied unchanged and still reads 'MKSNNALIVILGTVTLDAVG...' after the mutation, the codon deletion and the insertion. The extracted 5'-partial piece also carries the full-length protein. writeGenbank(out) exports that stale protein.

title: The contiguous-run rule contradicts the documented insertion rule, and the remapRange preview disagrees with insertBases
description:
Record edits (remapFeaturesWithPlan → remapSegments/absorbingSegment) treat adjacent segments as one stretch. Inserted bases at the junction of two adjacent segments are absorbed into one of them. This includes an origin-crossing feature in GenBank join form [s,L)+[0,e), the most common multi-segment feature on plasmids.

Three public statements still describe the per-segment rule:
- The spec: "a segment [s,e) with e <= gap is unchanged".
- The TSDoc of insertBases ("e <= gap -> unchanged") and the edit.ts header ("insertion at a boundary does not [extend]").
- The TSDoc of the preview API remapRange: "with the same rules as a feature segment".

remapRange cannot see neighbouring segments, so a UI that previews a feature segment by segment shows a different result than the committed edit. The run behaviour is scientifically defensible, since adjacent segments cover one contiguous stretch. The problem is that it is an undocumented spec deviation and the preview API is inconsistent with it. The implementer's own property "agree with the record edits" fails on this (seed 4001 case #1660).
expected: Pick one rule and state it everywhere. Either the spec's per-segment rule, or the run rule documented in the spec deviation list, insertBases's TSDoc and remapRange's TSDoc. In addition, the preview API (remapRange, or a run-aware variant) should give the same segment images as the committed edit.
actual: insertBases(lin, 5, 'TT') gives [0,7),[7,12) while its TSDoc and the spec say [0,5),[7,12). On the circular join, remapRange previews [18,20),[0,3) while insertBases produces [18,21),[0,3).

title: ops test suite is red (8 failing tests) and ops files fail tsc, contrary to the report
description:
In the current tree the module's own suite fails, and so does the typecheck. The report claims "133 tests in 10 files, all passing" and "ops files typecheck with 0 errors"; the task rules require own files error-free and tests green.

Seven failures are in ops.property.test.ts:
- insertBases token model: seed 1001 case 1953
- carried features: seed 1002 case 452
- sticky ends: seed 1501 case 9
- deleteRange: seed 2001 case 2
- replaceRange: seed 3001 case 8
- record replacement: seed 3003 case 8
- remap API agreement: seed 4001 case 1660

These tests' model predates two rules that remap.ts now implements:
- **Contiguous-run absorption.** On a circular record of L=234 with f0 = [107,111)+[233,234)+[0,192), inserting 12 bases at gap 0 grows segment [233,234) to [233,246). On a linear record of L=3 with segments [0,2),[1,2),[2,3), inserting 1 base at gap 2 grows [1,2) to [1,3). The spec's literal rule says such a segment (e <= gap) is unchanged. remapRange([1,2)) still returns [1,2), so its TSDoc claim of "the same rules as a feature segment" no longer holds.
- **/codon_start rewriting.** On a circular record of L=144, a strand -1 CDS [83,177) gains codon_start=2 after deleteRange [1,123). The property test's "non-positional fields unchanged" check fails on this.

Each forCases loop throws at its first failing case. So for 7 of the 18 property groups, covering every edit operation, most of the 2,500 cases (properties (a), (d), (e) and the sticky-end model) no longer run.

The eighth failure is the regression test "extractRange cannot take the parentRange of a plasmid cut once". It expects extractRange(pUC19, EcoRI fragment parentRange {284,2974}) not to throw. extractRange's TSDoc and checkRange deliberately reject ranges longer than the circle, so it throws a RangeError. The deliverable contradicts itself here. Cloning code that follows digest's documented parentRange for a vector cut once hits that RangeError.

On the behaviour itself: I checked the new rules with an independent run-aware per-base model (more than 66,000 cases), a codon-frame model and a qualifier-movement model, and found no behavioural error. The defect is the red, self-contradicting suite, which no longer verifies the edit operations.
expected: `npx vitest run src/ops` is all green, and `tsc` reports no errors in src/ops. The property tests, the regression tests and the code describe the same rules: either the per-segment rule or the run rule, and either extractRange accepts a parentRange longer than the circle or it does not.
actual: 8 of 149 tests fail (7 property groups plus 1 regression test), and there is 1 TS6133 error in src/ops/ops.regression.test.ts. The property groups for insert, delete, replace, record payloads, sticky ends and the remap API stop at their first failing case.

title: rotateOrigin(k) then rotateOrigin(L-k) is not the identity with position-bearing qualifiers: /transl_except rewritten, /rpt_unit_range silently dropped
description:
Spec property (f) requires that rotating by k and then by L-k is the identity, modulo ids. The qualifier remapping in qualifiers.ts breaks it in three ways.

**1. Split codons are never re-merged.** remapLocation merges consecutive bases only when they come from the same original run (`prev.run === b.run`). A codon that the first rotation splits across the origin is written as join(33,1..2) and is never merged again. So /transl_except=(pos:7..9,aa:Sec) comes back as (pos:join(7,8..9),aa:Sec); /anticodon behaves the same way.

**2. /rpt_unit_range and /tag_peptide are dropped.** remapValue returns null for these when their bases straddle the new origin (`out.loc.runs.length !== 1`). The annotation is lost without a warning, and rotating back cannot restore it: rotate(14) then rotate(L-14) deletes /rpt_unit_range=13..18.

**3. One-base ranges lose their ".." form.** formatLocation writes a one-base run without "..". So any remap, even a single reverseComplementRecord, turns /rpt_unit_range=12..12 into "12". INSDC defines <base_range> as a "location descriptor for a simple range of bases" written a..b, e.g. 202..245. As a side effect, reverseComplementRecord applied twice is no longer the identity, although the module's own property test asserts it for records without such qualifiers.

Measured on 4,000 random circular records from test-helpers' randomRecord with {positional: 1, joins: 0.3}:
- 1,514 rotate round trips differed from the input.
- 1,310 double reverse complements differed.
- 166 of the rotate round trips lost a /rpt_unit_range.

The existing (f) property test passes only because its generator never adds position-bearing qualifiers.
expected: The round trips return the input unchanged (spec property (f)): /transl_except stays (pos:7..9,aa:Sec), /rpt_unit_range=13..18 survives, and /rpt_unit_range=12..12 stays 12..12.
actual: All three tests fail. The /transl_except value becomes "(pos:join(7,8..9),aa:Sec)". The /rpt_unit_range qualifier list comes back as [], so the qualifier was dropped. The one-base range "12..12" becomes "12".

title: Position-bearing qualifier locations are expanded base by base: a 36 KB /transl_except makes rotateOrigin take 10.8 s and about 3 GB on a 10 kb plasmid
description:
remapLocation creates one MappedBase object for every base of every run (`for (let x = run.first; x <= run.last; x++) mapped.push({...})`). parseLocation accepts any number of runs, each as long as the whole record, overlapping or repeated.

So rotateOrigin, reverseComplementRecord, extractRange, concatRecords and insertBases with a record payload cost time and memory proportional to the total number of bases the qualifier text names. That total is unbounded: it does not depend on the file size or the record length. Parsing such a file is fast, so the freeze comes later, when the user sets the origin, reverse-complements or extracts.

Measurements on a 10 kb circular record whose CDS carries /transl_except=(pos:join(1..10000,…),aa:Sec):

| Runs | Value length | rotateOrigin | Memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | 3,618 chars | about 0.5 s | 350–640 MB heap |
| 4,000 | 36,018 chars | 10.8 s | 2,987 MB heapUsed, 3.3 GB max RSS |

Doubling the value would exceed a typical 4 GB webview heap and crash the app.

On the real E. coli genome, parsed with io/genbank, adding ten features with /rpt_unit_range=1..4641652 makes:
- rotateOrigin take 8.5 s
- reverseComplementRecord take 9.5 s
- extractRange take 8.0 s

That is about 0.9 s per qualifier, while the same operations take 4–211 ms without them.

Valid INSDC values name 1 to 3 bases (codon, anticodon) or one short range, so per-run arithmetic (shift, flip and split at the origin, O(runs)) or a cap on runs and bases would avoid this. Today a malformed or crafted file freezes the app or exhausts its memory.
expected: Work grows with the length of the qualifier text or the number of runs. Rotating a 10 kb record should take well under 100 ms and a few MB of memory, as it does without the qualifier.
actual: rotateOrigin took 10,842 ms with heapUsed 2,987 MB and a maximum RSS of 3,318,852 KB, and the test failed with "expected 10841.72 to be less than 100". On E. coli, ten /rpt_unit_range=1..4641652 qualifiers made rotateOrigin take 8,524 ms, reverseComplementRecord 9,491 ms and extractRange 7,998 ms.

title: Negative zero still leaks: remapGap returns -0, and addFeature/updateFeature store a -0 segment end or a -0 strand
description:
The module treats -0 as an invariant violation:
- checkGap and checkRange apply plusZero.
- The regression test "a gap of -0 produces -0 coordinates" pins that.
- rangeProblem and recordProblems in test-helpers flag -0.

Three paths still leak it:
1. **remapGap** validates the caret with checkGap and then discards the cleaned value (`checkGap(gap, oldLength, 'remapGap'); return remapGapWithPlan(plan, gap, bias).gap;`). A caret of Math.round(-0.3), which is -0 (the case the implementer cites), therefore comes back as -0 for any edit to its right. On linear records this goes through `off < 0 ? p : ...`; on circular records through newBaseIndex(plan, -0) and then mod(-0, n), which is -0.
2. **checkRange on circular records** returns `end` without plusZero. So addFeature and updateFeature on a circular record store {start: 0, end: -0}.
3. **validFeature** in crud.ts accepts strand -0 (because -0 === 0) and stores it. The implementer's own recordProblems then reports "feature f has strand -0".

The -0 surfaces in UI code through Object.is, toLocaleString ("-0") and Map keys.
expected: remapGap returns +0, the stored segment end is +0, and the stored strand is +0, so recordProblems reports nothing.
actual: All four tests fail. Both remapGap calls return -0 ("expected true to be false"). The stored segment end is -0. recordProblems reports ["feature f has strand -0"].

title: remapGap ignores bias 'right' at the left boundary of a replaced region: the caret lands before the typed text
description:
GapBias is documented as "Which side of the inserted bases a gap goes to when it sits exactly at the insertion point", with 'right' meaning "after them (e.g. a caret after typing)". For a replacement, the inserted bases go exactly at range.start. Yet remapGapWithPlan sends the left-boundary gap to insertAt whatever the bias (`else if (off === 0) out = insertAt;`), while a gap one base further right, strictly inside the region, honours 'right'.

The viewer's SequenceSelection sets caret = range.start for a selection made right to left. A UI that follows the GapBias doc and keeps the caret with remapGap(sel.caret, edit, L, topology, 'right') therefore puts the caret before the first replacement base. Each later keystroke is inserted in front of it: typing "ABC" over a backward selection produces "BCA".

The boundary rule is mentioned in remapGap's TSDoc, but it contradicts the GapBias definition and the "caret after typing" example. The API offers no bias that puts a boundary caret after a replacement; the caller has to compute plan.insertAt + plan.inserted itself.
expected: remapGap(2, replace [2,5) with 3 bases, 'right') returns 5, after the inserted bases, the same as a gap strictly inside the region.
actual: It returns 2, before the inserted bases ("expected 2 to be 5"). Only the left-boundary gap ignores the bias.
